title: A benchmarking protocol for intact protein-level Tandem Mass Tag (TMT) labeling for quantitative top-down proteomics☆
author: Guo, Yu, et al.
materials: Detailed procedure is shown in in Supplementary Document.

Proteins bound on trapping column are then eluted onto a C5 RPLC capillary column using a modified Thermo Scientific (Waltham, MA, USA.) Accela LC system for seperation [5,8]. A 200-min gradient from 10% to 70% of MPB is applied for protein separation at a flow rate of 400 nL/min. The LC eluent is analyzed by an Orbitrap Exploris 240 mass spectrometer in positive mode (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) using a customized nano-ESI interface [3]. 3.4.

steps.title: Prepare Mobile Phase A Buffer
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, prepare 1 L of Mobile Phase A (MPA) by adding 50 mL LC‑MS grade acetonitrile, 25 mL LC‑MS grade isopropanol, and 920 mL LC‑MS grade water to a 1000 mL storage bottle; then add 5.85 mL glacial acetic acid and 0.1 mL Pierce™ TFA using a glass pipette, sonicate for 15 min, and store at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Wear gloves, goggles, and lab coat while preparing the buffer.
Use only glass pipettes for TFA to avoid reaction with plastic.

steps.title: Prepare Mobile Phase B Buffer
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, prepare 1 L of Mobile Phase B (MPB) by adding 450 mL acetonitrile, 450 mL isopropanol, and 95 mL water to a 1000 mL storage bottle; then add 5.85 mL glacial acetic acid and 0.1 mL TFA with a glass pipette, sonicate for 15 min, and store at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Wear gloves, goggles, and lab coat while preparing the buffer.
Use only glass pipettes for TFA to avoid reaction with plastic.

steps.title: Dilute and Load TMT‑Labeled Protein
steps.instruction: Dilute the TMT‑labeled protein sample with HPLC water until the organic solvent percentage is below 10 %; load exactly 10 µg of this diluted sample onto the home‑packed C5 trapping column (150 µm i.d., 5 cm) at a flow rate of 5–8 µL min⁻¹ for 20 min.

steps.title: Perform LC Separation and MS Acquisition
steps.instruction: Elute bound proteins from the trapping column onto the home‑packed C5 RPLC capillary column (75 µm i.d., 70 cm) using a Thermo Accela LC system; apply a 200‑min linear gradient from 10 % to 70 % MPB at 400 nL min⁻¹, and analyze the eluate on an Orbitrap Exploris 240 in positive nano‑ESI mode.

steps.title: Set Orbitrap Exploris 240 Parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the mass spectrometer as follows: inlet capillary temperature = 275 °C; spray voltage = 2.6 kV; full MS scans (500–2000 m/z) at 120 000 resolution with 3 microscans; select top 6 most abundant precursors (charge 4–50) for MS/MS; MS/MS scans (100–1600 m/z) at 120 000 resolution with 2 microscans, 2.0 m/z isolation window, 20 s dynamic exclusion; HCD normalized energy = 35 %; maximum injection times = 1000 ms (full) and 500 ms (MS/MS); AGC targets = 3 × 10⁶ (full) and 1 × 10⁶ (MS/MS).

steps.title: Convert Raw Files to mzML
steps.instruction: Use MSconvert to convert all Orbitrap raw files to mzML format before downstream processing.

steps.title: Deconvolute Spectra with TopFD
steps.instruction: Run TopFD on the mzML files with the following parameters: MS1 signal‑to‑noise ratio = 3, MS2 signal‑to‑noise ratio = 1, precursor window size = 3.0 m/z, maximum mass = 50 000 Da, maximum charge = 30, m/z error tolerance = 0.02 Da; all other settings remain at default.

steps.title: Identify Proteoforms with TopPIC
steps.instruction: Search the TopFD output with TopPIC against the UniProt Human database (release 2021‑05‑14, 20 380 entries) using decoy‑based FDR = 0.01 at spectrum and proteoform levels; allow up to 2 mass shifts within ±500 Da; provide a fixed‑modification file containing the PTMs listed in Table 1 (acetylation + 42.0106 Da on K, carboxymethyl + 58.0055 Da on C, phosphorylation + 79.9663 Da on S/T/Y, oxidation + 15.9949 Da on M, etc., and TMT‑6plex + 229.1629 Da on K and N‑termini).

steps.title: Quantify TMT Reporter Ions
steps.instruction: Take the buffer‑exchanged protein sample from the LC step, split it into four equal aliquots and label each with a different TMT‑6plex tag (127, 128, 130, 131); mix the labeled aliquots at a mass ratio of 5 : 2 : 1 : 1; acquire LC‑MS/MS data; extract reporter‑ion intensities from the mzML files using the previously described in‑house Python script; compute normalized intensity ratios 127/131, 128/131, and 130/131 and compare them to the theoretical ratio 5 : 2 : 1 (observed ratios: 5.00 ± 1.37, 1.97 ± 0.76, 1.05 ± 0.34).

steps.title: Visualize Proteoform Spectra in ProSight Lite
steps.instruction: Load the protein mass list, precursor monoisotopic mass, and sequence for a protein of interest (e.g., cyclin‑dependent kinase regulatory subunit 1, UniProt P61024) into ProSight Lite; manually assign the PTMs and TMT tags from Table 1 to obtain the best matching fragmentation pattern; confirm identification and assess quantification from reporter‑ion intensities.
